questions.q: What determines whether a journal needs approval, and from whom?
options: Every journal always needs the same single approver
Only the journal's currency
Whether the journal was created before or after noon
Approval rules that evaluate the journal's attributes such as ledger, source, category, amount, and preparer
questions.explain: Approval rules evaluate a journal's business attributes to decide if and how it routes for approval.

questions.q: In a parallel assignee routing, what is required for the journal to move forward?
options: Only one of the assigned people needs to approve
Approvers must act one after another in sequence
Everyone in the parallel set must approve
No approval is ever required
questions.explain: Parallel assignees all work at once, and every one of them must approve.

questions.q: What is a serial assignee routing most commonly used for?
options: Routing to a random user
A supervisory chain, where approvers act one after another in sequence
Routing only to system accounts
Skipping approval entirely
questions.explain: Serial assignees typically follow a supervisory chain, approving in order.

questions.q: Where are General Ledger journal approval rules configured?
options: In the Business Process Management Worklist application (or via a simplified spreadsheet configuration)
Inside the Create Journal screen directly
In the chart of accounts setup
They cannot be configured — they are fixed by Oracle
questions.explain: Approval rules are configured in BPM Worklist, with a simplified spreadsheet-based option also available.

questions.q: Where can you check exactly which stage and approver a submitted journal is currently waiting on?
options: The Period Close checklist
The chart of accounts value set
Manage Journal Approvals
The Scheduled Processes monitor only
questions.explain: Manage Journal Approvals shows a journal's current approval status, stage, and approver.
